questions: Should the function raise an error if the DataFrame contains any NaN values, or should it silently propagate NaN through covariance and pair plot?
Should the covariance matrix be computed using the default pandas covariance method (unbiased estimator, ddof=1) or a different method (e.g., population covariance, ddof=0)?
Should the pair plot include a diagonal (e.g., histograms, KDE) and off-diagonal (e.g., scatter plots) as default seaborn pairplot, or should any specific plot types be enforced?
Should the function return the covariance matrix as a DataFrame with column/row labels matching the input DataFrame's column names (after any duplicate handling), or is any labeling acceptable?
If the input DataFrame has a single column, should the pair plot still be generated (a 1x1 grid with a single plot), or should it be handled differently (e.g., raise error or return None)?
Should the function modify the input DataFrame (e.g., in-place operations) or leave it unchanged?
Should the function accept optional parameters for seaborn pairplot (e.g., hue, palette, markers) to be passed through, or strictly use defaults?
Should the covariance matrix be computed on the original data or after any potential automatic data transformations (e.g., standardization) within the pair plot?
